summary: The first draft now has 97 screens in 16 groups, built on Journey's design system (Sun, glass, Plus Jakarta Sans, the same components). The last three groups are new, drawn from your first three comments: Jot (adding things without opening the app), Keepsakes (more like the time capsule) and Fair and fun (more like the chore wheel). The hub also answers your three questions: a name, how the two apps tie together, and whether they should share a database and a server. Nothing is built yet and nothing here is decided.
next: Look at the three new groups at the end of the **Screens**: 14 *Jot*, 15 *Keepsakes*, 16 *Fair and fun*. Tell me which you love, which to drop, and what is still missing.
Carry on through the rest of the **Screens** and comment on anything. Group 10, *With Journey*, and the sheet screens in group 8 are the ones I most want your eye on.
Try the names with the **Name** switch on the Screens page, then read *The name*. Tell me which feel right, or give me words you like.
Read *The two apps, together* and tell me which links matter most to you. Some need small changes inside Journey.
Answer the seven questions under *What it does*. Two of them shape the build: how private is private, and whether there is a paid plan.
To let me reply inside a comment thread and close it, send the thread to Claude (reply on it with Send to Claude). Your first three are answered by the new screens but stay open until then.

open.a: An iPhone will not keep a notification for ever or take typing inside a widget; an Android phone does more. I drew what each can really do: on iPhone a pinned note you press and hold to type in (it returns after each add), one-tap chips and ticks in widgets, voice, the Action Button and the share sheet. Is that close enough to what you pictured, or should the iPhone side lean harder on one of them?
My pick is Porchlight. Hearth would have been perfect and is taken by a family organiser. None of the names has had a trademark, store or domain check yet.

In this draft only the Vault is scrambled so that the service can't read it. Notes, photos and files are private to the people you choose but readable by the service, so that search inside scans, reminders from documents and moments can work. Scrambling everything is possible and switches those off.
Keeping a family's full-size photos and videos costs roughly US$0.75 to 3 a month per family. A free amount with a family plan is the usual answer. The numbers are yours to set.
All six places is several apps' worth of work. I suggest: circles and sharing, then Library, Plan, Notes, Money, Vault, in that order, each one going to a few test families before the next.
Today, Plan, Notes, Library, Money, Vault. Are these the right six, in the right order? Is anything you'd use daily more than one tap away?
Grouping photos by who is in them is powerful and sensitive, most of all with children. On the phone only, off by default, or not at all? The draft leaves it out.
Send a booking, a bill or a school letter to the circle's own address and it arrives as an event or a bill. It needs a mail-receiving service that Journey doesn't have. First version, or later?

updates.text: After your first three comments: 22 more screens. **Jot** (8): widgets, a note pinned in notifications that you type into, voice, the share button, and how each phone's limits are handled. **Keepsakes** (7): Open when…, the birthday interview, Things they said, Same spot every year, Grandma's stories, the good things jar, the doorframe. **Fair and fun** (6): Whose turn?, the piggy bank, secret missions, the Saturday jar, Sleeps until…, Where is it?. Plus *Goodnight from far away* in the Journey group.

First draft: the hub, 75 screens in 13 groups, the design system copied from Journey's Design 2.1, a name shortlist with a switch on every screen, the link with Journey, the requirements, and the answer on sharing a database and a server.
